newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge higher in narrow trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge higher in narrow trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares ended barely higher on Monday in thin and highly selective trade amid political uncertainty still haunting the market, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed three points, or 0.2 percent higher at 1,470 after moving between 1,452 and 1,480. It had lost 1.7 percent last week.
Trade volume firmed to 13.43 trillion lira ($96.4 million) from Friday's 12.03 trillion ($86.8 million).
Brokers said weak volume and caution caused activity to concentrate on three bluechip utilities for the second day in a row. They made up 33.2 percent of the total turnover.
"The market will set direction according to developments concerning the fate of the government," said Ibrahim Basnur from Ar securities.

"It will be relieved if the government falls because the coalition has not been able to take any radical decisions in the past three-four months. There has been no solid progress in vital structural reforms, particularly privatisation," he added.
Four MPs from the secularist wing of the Islamist-conservative coalition have resigned since last Tuesday when the government survived a censure motion in parliament by a close vote.
